hair_dryer_nocup-s2-B.sheet:
## In-use pose
- The backplate lies flat against a vertical wall. The wall is the plane y = 0; the wall normal is +y, pointing out into the room.
- Z is up. The holder's lowest point is z = 0 (plate bottom edge). The plate's back face sits on y = 0.
- The user stands on the +y side. The ring opening faces along +x (horizontal, parallel to the wall), so the dryer slides in sideways.
- The plate is fixed by two screws through two holes along +y. The holes sit outside the ring footprint.
- The ring axis is parallel to the wall (along x). A triangular profile bracket in the yz plane carries the ring off the plate face.

## Variant B: wall-parallel ring on bracket
Read of the brief: "ring plane parallel to the wall" is taken as the ring axis lying parallel to the wall, per the shared assumption "ring axis parallel to the wall". The annular faces are therefore perpendicular to the wall.

## Geometry (all mm)
- Backplate: 120 (x) x 5 (y, thickness) x 140 (z). Origin at (0,0,0).
- Ring: tube, axis x, length 40 (ring depth), outer diameter 100 (ring wall 5), bore 90. Centred on the plate in x and z, so x 40..80 and z 20..120. Axis at y = 75.
- Bracket: triangular profile in the yz plane, extruded 40 along x (same span as the ring). Vertices in (y,z): (5,45), (5,95), (27.5,70). The base lies on the plate front face (y = 5). The apex (y = 27.5) sits inside the ring wall at mid-wall radius 47.5 from the axis.
- Screw holes: two through holes, d = 4.5 (M4 clearance), along y, centred at x = 15 and x = 105, z = 70. Both lie outside the ring footprint (x 40..80).

## Placement arithmetic
- Ring axis y = plate_t + standoff = 5 + 70 = 75. Position y = 75 - 50 = 25.
- Ring position x = (120 - 40)/2 = 40. Position z = 70 - 50 = 20.
- Bracket position: x = 40, y = 5 (plate face), z = 70 - 25 = 45.

## Checks
- Ring bore 90 clears the dryer body (the envelope is drawn at 90).
- Bounding box: x 0..120, y 0..125, z 0..140, which matches the component union.
- Hole inset 15 + 2.25 < ring_x 40, so the holes clear the ring footprint.
- Bracket apex y 27.5 > plate face y 5, so the bracket joins the plate and the ring.

## Open items (user to confirm)
- Plate width/height/thickness, hole diameter and spacing, ring wall and depth, and ring orientation are all set to the nominal values above.
- Ring is centred on the plate.
- The bracket profile points are fixed to the nominal standoff (70) and half-base (25); regenerate them if those change.

hair_dryer_holder-s0-B.sheet:
## In-use pose
- The backplate lies flat against a vertical wall. The wall is the plane y = 0; the plate occupies x 0..140 and z 0..150 and is 5 mm thick along +Y, away from the wall.
- Up is +Z. The lowest point of the model is the plate bottom edge at z = 0.
- The user faces the front of the plate (+Y side). The cup ring projects straight out from the plate front face along +Y, so its axis is normal to the wall and its opening faces away from the wall.
- Two M4 clearance through-holes (axis Y) fix the plate to the wall. They sit near the bottom edge, at z = 12, at x = 30 and x = 110.
- The dryer barrel or nozzle rests horizontally inside the 90 mm bore, with its axis along Y. A retaining ledge sits under the ring floor, between the plate face and the ring front, to resist the dryer sliding out.

## Parameters (assembly mm)
- plate_w = 140 (plate width along X)
- plate_h = 150 (plate height along Z)
- plate_t = 5 (plate thickness along Y)
- hole_d = 4.5 (M4 clearance through-hole)
- hole_spacing = 80 (centre-to-centre, along X)
- hole_z = 12 (hole centre height above the wall-plate bottom)
- bore_d = 90 (ring inner diameter, user-stated, pinned)
- wall = 8 (ring wall radial thickness)
- ring_h = 25 (ring axial length along Y)
- ledge_w = 30 (ledge width along X)
- ledge_h = 15 (ledge depth below the ring outer bottom)

## Derived
- ring_od = bore_d + 2*wall = 106
- ring_r = ring_od / 2 = 53
- ring_cx = plate_w / 2 = 70 (ring axis X)
- ring_cz = plate_h / 2 = 75 (ring axis Z)
- hole_x1 = plate_w/2 - hole_spacing/2 = 30
- hole_x2 = plate_w/2 + hole_spacing/2 = 110
- ledge top = ring_cz - ring_r + wall = 30 (ledge meets the ring bore bottom line, no intrusion into the 90 mm bore)

## Components
1. backplate: box 140 x 150 x 5 at the origin. Two through holes along Y at (30, 12) and (110, 12), d 4.5. Sharp edges.
2. cup_ring: tube along Y, outer diameter 106, inner bore 90, length 25. Placed with its local min corner at (17, 5, 22), so its axis is at x = 70, z = 75. Its back face touches the plate front face at y = 5. Full closed ring, sharp edges.
3. retaining_ledge: box 30 (X) x 25 (Y) x 23 (Z). Placed at (55, 5, 7). It spans from the plate front face (y = 5) to the ring front (y = 30). Its top at z = 30 lies inside the ring bottom wall, so the bore stays clear. Its bottom at z = 7 is above the ground plane.

## Clearances and checks
- Ring bore 90 mm is an open circle: no obstruction inside the bore from the plate face (the plate face is flat at y = 5 and is not inside the bore).
- Holes at (30, 12) and (110, 12): distance from ring axis to hole centre is sqrt(40^2 + 63^2) = 74.6, which exceeds ring_r + hole_r = 55.25. The holes clear the ring.
- Ledge bottom at z = 7 and plate bottom at z = 0, so the lowest point is z = 0.
- Bounding box: X 0..140, Y 0..30, Z 0..150.

## Joints
All parts are permanently joined by touching faces (ring to plate at y = 5, ledge to plate at y = 5 and to ring wall). No jointContract.

pen_holder-s0-A.sheet:
## In-use pose
The pen holder stands on its square base on a flat surface. The base bottom sits on the ground plane z = 0. The four tubes point straight up (+Z) from the top face of the base. Tube openings face up (+Z) at the top and down into the base at the bottom. Nothing is rotated. The user reaches in from above.

## Variant A: Literal four tubes on square base
- base: solid square plate, 80 x 80 mm in X and Y, base_t thick in Z (5 mm suggested), bottom face on z = 0. Occupies x 0..80, y 0..80, z 0..5.
- tubes: four open-ended vertical tubes, outer diameter tube_od = tube_id + 2 x wall = 20 + 2 x 2 = 24 mm, inner diameter 20 mm, height tube_h = 100 mm. Each tube stands on the base top face at z = base_t = 5 and reaches z = 105.
- tube layout: 2 x 2 grid. Tube centres inset 20 mm from each base edge, so centres sit at x = 20 and 60, y = 20 and 60. Tube min corners are at 20 - 12 = 8 and 60 - 12 = 48 in X and Y.
- tube bore: through-bore, open at top. The bore bottom is closed by the base plate, which is solid under each tube.
- joins: the tubes are permanently joined to the base (touching, sharing the base top face). No joint clearance.
- edges: sharp, no chamfers, fillets or rounds.
- no other features. No holes declared (no fasteners).

## Overall extents
- X: 0 .. 80 mm
- Y: 0 .. 80 mm
- Z: 0 .. 105 mm (base_t + tube_h)

## Checks
- tube_od 24 mm is larger than tube_id 20 mm (wall 2 mm).
- Each tube fits inside the footprint: tube_lo = 8 >= 0 and tube_hi + tube_od = 48 + 24 = 72 <= 80.
- Gap between adjacent tube outer walls: 40 - 24 = 16 mm.

headphone_hook_underdesk-s2-A.sheet:
## In-use pose
The hook is screwed flat to the underside of a desk. The desk is overhead, so up is toward the desk (+z). The plate's top face sits against the desk underside at z = 53. The vertical arm hangs down from the plate and the horizontal hook sits at the bottom, with its underside on the ground plane z = 0. The hook's tip points in +x, away from the plate's centre. The user stands on the -y side of the hook and faces +y, so the headband is hung on the hook from below.

## Geometry (all mm)
- Mounting plate: 60 x 40 x 3, local origin at its min corner, placed at [0, 0, 50]. Plate underside at z = 50, top at z = 53.
- Two through holes, 4.5 mm diameter, axis z, centred at x = 10 and x = 50, y = 20 (plate centreline). Both are 10 mm from the plate ends and clear of the arm.
- Vertical arm: 10 x 10 square bar, 50 long, from z = 0 to z = 50. Centred on the plate at x = 25 to 35, y = 15 to 25. Its top face touches the plate underside.
- Horizontal hook: 10 x 10 square bar, 40 long in +x, from the outer face of the arm at x = 35 to x = 75, at y = 15 to 25, z = 0 to 10. Its underside is on z = 0.

## Overall extents
- X: 0 to 75 (plate 0 to 60; hook tip 75)
- Y: 0 to 40 (plate width)
- Z: 0 to 53 (hook underside 0; plate top 53)

## Parts (3 free bodies, all box shapes)
1. mount_plate (with two through holes)
2. drop_arm
3. hook_tip (horizontal hook section, reads as the headband rest)

Permanently joined parts touch on shared faces. No jointContract.

## Fit checks
- Holes (x = 10 and 50, y = 20) clear the arm (x = 25 to 35) by 12.75 mm and 15 mm respectively, and lie wholly inside the plate.
- Hook reach 40 mm beyond the arm. The hook extends from x = 35 to x = 75.

## Open items (carried as assumptions)
- Plate thickness 3 mm, arm section 10 x 10 mm, hole diameter 4.5 mm, arm and hole placement, and hook direction are not stated in the request and are set as assumptions.
- Desk edge position is not given, so clearance to the desk edge is not verified here.

## Edges

pi_case-s2-A.sheet:
## In-use pose
The tray stands flat on a desk or shelf. Its floor bottom sits on z = 0 (ground plane). The open face of the tray points up (+z). The Raspberry Pi 4 board sits on four standoffs inside the tray, and the flat lid sits on top of the tray walls, closing the opening. The user looks at the assembly from the front (-y side); the board's long (85 mm) edge runs along x. No port cutouts are made (not requested).

## Fixed numbers (from the Raspberry Pi 4 published geometry and the brief)
- Board outline: 85 x 56 mm.
- Mounting-hole pattern: 58 x 49 mm rectangle, centred on the board.
- Mounting-hole bore: 2.75 mm diameter (M2.5 clearance).

## Placeholder numbers (brief shared assumptions)
- Wall thickness 2 mm, floor thickness 2 mm (floor bottom at z = 0).
- Tray wall height 20 mm above the floor top, so the tray is 22 mm tall overall.
- Standoff height 5 mm above the floor top; standoff outer diameter 6 mm.
- Lid: flat 2 mm plate matching the tray outer footprint.
- Cavity clearance 0 mm beyond the board footprint. All edges sharp.

## Derived footprint
- Tray outer: 85 + 2 x 2 = 89 mm (x) by 56 + 2 x 2 = 60 mm (y), 22 mm tall.
- Cavity (inside walls): 85 x 56 mm, x from 2 to 87, y from 2 to 58, z from 2 (floor top) upward.

## Standoff layout
Board centre in the tray is (44.5, 30). Standoff bore centres are at x = 44.5 +/- 29 -> 15.5 and 73.5; y = 30 +/- 24.5 -> 5.5 and 54.5. Each 6 mm standoff's local origin is its min corner, so origins are centre minus 3:
- pi_standoff_a: (12.5, 2.5)
- pi_standoff_b: (70.5, 2.5)
- pi_standoff_c: (12.5, 51.5)
- pi_standoff_d: (70.5, 51.5)
All four stand on the floor top at z = 2 and rise to z = 7. Each carries a 2.75 mm through bore.

## Board seating
The board rests on the four standoff tops at z = 7 (floor 2 + standoff 5). Board PCB thickness 1.5 mm is shown as a guide envelope only; the board is not built.

## Lid
Flat 89 x 60 x 2 mm plate at z = 22, sitting on the top edges of the four walls (tray top at z = 22). No skirt, no ledge, no clearance: lid and tray are a permanent-touch pair with no joint contract.

## Component list (6 free bodies)
1. pi_tray - open-top shell 89 x 60 x 22 mm, 2 mm walls and floor, open +Z.
2. pi_standoff_a - tube, 6 mm OD, 2.75 mm bore, 5 mm tall.
3. pi_standoff_b - tube, same.
4. pi_standoff_c - tube, same.
5. pi_standoff_d - tube, same.
6. pi_lid - flat plate 89 x 60 x 2 mm.

## Bounding box
89 x 60 x 24 mm (lid top at z = 24). Lowest x, y, z are all 0.

bike_hook_wall-s1-A.sheet:
## In-use pose
The hook is screwed to a vertical wall. The backplate lies flat against the wall face, so its face normal is horizontal (+Y points away from the wall). Up is +Z and z = 0 is the ground plane, which is the lowest point of the backplate. The user stands in front of the wall (+Y side). The arm projects horizontally in +Y from the wall face. Its opening, the space above the arm between the wall and the tip, faces up and toward the user. The three screw holes pass straight through the backplate along Y, entering from the wall face.

## Geometry (all mm)
- Wall face: plane Y = 0.
- Backplate: 80 along X (wall width), 4 along Y (thickness), 150 along Z (height). Occupies X 0..80, Y 0..4, Z 0..150.
- Three through-holes, d = 4.5 (M4 clearance), axis Y. Triangle layout in the backplate face: two at X = 20 and X = 60 on Z = 120, one at X = 40 on Z = 85. All holes stay above the arm root (Z > 60), so they do not cut the arm.
- Hook profile: an L-shaped outline in the YZ plane, extruded 20 along X (arm width). It is centred on the backplate: X 30..50.
  - Arm: Y 0..120 (120 mm from the wall face to the free end), Z 20..30 (10 thick). The arm root sits at Z = 20 above the ground plane.
  - Upturned tip: Y 110..120 (10 thick at the free end), Z 20..60. It rises 30 above the arm top (Z 30 to 60).
  - Profile points (Y, Z) relative to the hook origin: (0,0), (120,0), (120,40), (110,40), (110,10), (0,10). The root overlaps the backplate by 4 mm in Y, so the two bodies are joined.
- Overall bounding box: X 0..80, Y 0..120, Z 0..150.

## Joining
Backplate and hook are one solid. They are permanently joined at the wall face, so there is no joint clearance and no jointContract.

## Edges
All edges are sharp. No chamfers, fillets or rounds.

## Values not stated in the request (confirm before drafting)
Backplate thickness 4, arm section 20 wide by 10 thick, arm root height Z 20, tip thickness 10, screw hole d 4.5 with the triangle layout above.
